context:
Run each cloud verification in its own work unit / PR — failures on
one engine shouldn't block the others. For each engine: get creds
set up, run the supported sketch-op set, observe results, reconcile any
discrepancies, commit the corrected overrides and per-engine
tolerance bounds.

Tolerance bounds may need to be re-tuned per engine — this is the
same methodology used in the original PR #112 w5 (empirical
observation + wide-enough-to-not-false-fail, tight-enough-to-catch-
no-op). Document the engine name alongside the observed value in
the inline comment.

Function-signature corrections are landing-blockers for that engine
(the override is wrong if it doesn't run); document them prominently
in the PR.
description:
## Revalidated 2026-10-01: neither original blocker still applies

**(1) Cloud credentials — resolved for Snowflake, BigQuery and Databricks.** They are configured in ~/.benchbox/credentials.yaml and live runs against them are executing from develop. Redshift credentials are valid but the cluster is unreachable from the run host (connection timed out; tracked in approx-survey-remaining-legs), so Redshift stays out of the first pass.

**(2) validation_query per-platform overrides — the mechanism now exists, the cloud data does not.** `ValidationQuery.platform_overrides` is resolved in write_primitives/benchmark.py (`_resolve_validation_sql`; an explicit `null` skips that validation with a logged reason), and the catalog already uses it for ClickHouse and Redshift. The headline ★ ops still have no Snowflake, BigQuery or Databricks override for the validation SQL: for example `theta_estimate_in_range` in sketch_query_theta_union_merge overrides only clickhouse and redshift, so on the three cloud engines it runs the DuckDB-only `datasketch_*` SQL and raises "unknown function" after a write that actually succeeded. Writing those overrides is part of this item: author a Snowflake, BigQuery and Databricks validation override (or an explicit null skip) for each sketch op whose validation SQL is DuckDB-specific, before judging any cloud run.

Per-engine scope:
  - **Redshift** (later): PR #134 added 4 HLL-substitution overrides (DDL, theta-style insert, theta-style merge, drop). Tolerance bounds for the merged HLL distinct estimate were authored against DataSketches Theta and may need re-tuning to absorb HLL++ bias; see the PR #134 description for the conservative starting bounds.
  - **ClickHouse Cloud**: the ClickHouse-native -State/-Merge overrides are done (write-primitives-sketch-clickhouse-and-storage-metrics); run them when ClickHouse Cloud credentials exist.

Resolution path:
  1. Add the missing cloud validation overrides and unit-test that each is resolved for its platform.
  2. Run each sketch op on Snowflake, BigQuery and Databricks, each engine in its own work unit and PR, with an explicit live-run approval stating command, maximum runtime, log path and stop condition.
  3. Reconcile function names, signatures and tolerance bounds with observed behavior; record the engine alongside each observed value.

## Original description

The merged write_primitives sketch category shipped with
`platform_overrides` for Snowflake, BigQuery, and Databricks
written from documented function names but **never executed against
real cloud engines**. Cloud credentials weren't available locally
during the original implementation, and the hard-block protocol
permitted DuckDB-with-extension coverage as the merge-test
acceptance criterion.

This TODO is the verification follow-up: run each sketch op against
each cloud engine and reconcile any discrepancies between the
documented function names / signatures and the actual engine behavior.

anti_patterns.dont: bundle multi-engine verification into a single PR
anti_patterns.instead: one PR per engine, each with its own w1/w2/w3 work unit.
anti_patterns.why: failures on one engine should not block the others

anti_patterns.dont: keep DuckDB-derived expected_value bounds for cloud engines that produce meaningfully different estimates
anti_patterns.instead: re-tune per engine and document the per-engine values inline.
anti_patterns.why: that would false-fail healthy cloud sketches

anti_patterns.dont: loosen DuckDB bounds to accommodate cloud bias
anti_patterns.instead: keep DuckDB bounds tight and add per-engine bounds as separate annotations.
anti_patterns.why: DuckDB's tighter bounds are a real correctness signal

anti_patterns.instead: fix the override or remove it with a documented `# verified missing on $engine` comment.
anti_patterns.why: the failure indicates a function-signature drift that future readers should know about

preserves.behavior: ClickHouse sketch ops (added by `write-primitives-sketch-clickhouse-and-storage-metrics` if landed first) continue to pass — cloud verification doesn't touch ClickHouse.
Existing DuckDB sketch ops continue to pass with their current scalar-bounds validation contracts (cloud-tuning re-tunes per-engine bounds, not the DuckDB ones).

work_units.notes:
Run sketch ops on a small Snowflake warehouse (XS or smaller is
fine for SF=0.01). Confirm 8/8 pass with the existing override
SQL. If DATASKETCHES_THETA_* function names diverge from current
Snowflake docs, update the override and document the corrected
signature in the cross-platform doc.

Critical-path checks:
  - APPROX_TOP_K_ACCUMULATE(l_shipmode, 1024) produces a sketch
    that combines correctly via APPROX_TOP_K_COMBINE.
  - DATASKETCHES_THETA_ACCUMULATE handles the INTEGER cast for
    l_extendedprice without precision loss.
  - kll_sketch_agg's quantile-estimate handles the merged
    sketch correctly (Snowflake uses different KLL bindings
    than the C++ DataSketches library).

Output: per-op result JSON committed somewhere appropriate
(or summarised in the PR description); inline tolerance comments
updated with Snowflake observations.
work_units.summary: Snowflake: live verification of all 8 sketch ops; reconcile any function-signature discrepancies

work_units.notes:
Run 6 sketch ops (skip the 2 topk ops which have `bigquery: null`)
on a real BigQuery project. Confirm HLL_COUNT.INIT / .MERGE
semantics produce the expected distinct count via the persist+
merge loop.

Critical-path checks:
  - HLL_COUNT.INIT(x) produces a BYTES sketch that round-trips
    through table storage.
  - HLL_COUNT.MERGE(sketch_column) implicitly merges across rows
    (no separate ACCUMULATE step needed in BigQuery — verify
    this matches our override structure).
  - KLL_QUANTILES.INIT_INT64 + MERGE_POINT_INT64 produces the
    expected median for l_extendedprice (note the INT64 cast —
    may lose decimal precision; confirm the median is still
    meaningful).

Also revisit: is there actually a top-K accumulator in BigQuery
that we missed? APPROX_TOP_COUNT is documented as one-shot, but
check for any newer functions.
work_units.summary: BigQuery: live verification of 6 sketch ops (skip topk pair); confirm HLL substitution behavior

work_units.notes:
Run sketch ops on a small Databricks warehouse / SQL endpoint
/ cluster. Critical-path checks:
  - theta_sketch_agg vs hll_sketch_agg: Databricks' DataSketches
    integration may default to one or the other; confirm the
    override matches the function actually available in the
    target DBR.
  - approx_top_k_accumulate availability depends on DBR Spark
    version; if DBR is < Spark 4.1 equivalent, the topk ops will
    fail with "function not found" — guard with a runtime
    version check or accept the fail and skip.
  - Photon path: are sketch UDAFs Photonised? If not, expect
    slower latency than the SQL claims would suggest.
work_units.summary: Databricks: live verification of all 8 sketch ops on Databricks Runtime

work_units.notes:
Run the 4 Redshift HLL-substitution ops added by PR #134:

  - sketch_ddl_create_persistent_table
  - sketch_insert_theta_per_partition
  - sketch_query_theta_union_merge
  - sketch_drop_persistent_table

Critical-path checks:
  - HLL_CREATE_SKETCH returns HLLSKETCH values that persist to
    table storage and merge via HLL_COMBINE.
  - HLL_CARDINALITY(HLL_COMBINE(...)) lands inside the tightened
    starting tolerance [14500, 15500] for SF=0.01's 15000
    distinct l_orderkeys, or the bounds are re-tuned with
    observed live values documented inline.
  - HLLSKETCH columns are not used as DISTKEY / SORTKEY, and do
    not appear in GROUP BY / ORDER BY / DISTINCT positions.

Output: Redshift runtime version, driver version, observed HLL
cardinality, and any DDL restriction drift documented in
operations.yaml comments and the cross-platform sketch doc.
work_units.summary: Redshift: live verification of 4 HLL-substitution sketch ops

work_units.notes:
For each engine that completed verification, append a one-line
comment to its platform_overrides block noting the runtime
version and date verified (e.g. "# Snowflake: verified
2026-MM-DD against driver 3.x.y, function names confirmed").

This makes future regressions easier to triage — if an op breaks
after a Snowflake driver upgrade, the comment shows when it
last worked.
work_units.summary: Update operations.yaml inline comments with verified-against-runtime-version notes
